thesis: MR D.I.Y. retains a plausible recovery case, but its quoted 5.32% yield is not fully supported by the conservative H1 cash bridge. The bear carries the payout-quality objection: RM511.784m dividends exceed RM462.958m cash after the specified capex, leases and interest, while quarterly net margin fell to 10.69%. Positive operating cash and 17.71x trailing earnings preserve upside, so this supports waiting rather than a demonstrated business-value sell.
strongest_counterexample: Even mechanically removing the RM124.040m inventory release leaves RM338.918m positive adjusted cash, and H1 revenue grew 6.46% with operating profit broadly flat; recovery has real financing resources.
invalidation_conditions: A subsequent comparable H1 with dividends no greater than cash after the same capex/lease/interest bridge, and quarterly attributable-profit/revenue margin at least the prior 13.06%, would defeat the present wait thesis.
Negative cash after the same bridge in the next comparable H1, from positive RM462.958m, would require a more bearish ruling.
decisive_factors: Payout coverage is a disclosed cash dispute, not a missing-data problem.
Lease-inclusive net debt RM1.411bn and inventory-supported CFO make recurring yield quality material.
